summary.en: Drone attacks from Sudan now dominate the lethal landscape, with Sudanese drones responsible for nearly three quarters of war deaths this year, and South Sudan accusing Sudan of a drone strike that killed scores in a disputed area. Violence continues domestically, including a road ambush in Warrap that killed five people, a plane crash at Juba Airport that left three survivors, and a woman allegedly beaten over an SPLM primary vote. Machar urged a special court to deploy unified forces to Nasir before the 2025 clashes, while the governor of Jonglei province reported efforts to end deadly clashes in Bor, Duk and Twic East. New regulatory moves include the SSRA and NCA tightening betting and gambling company rules, and the NEC briefing an AU electoral expert on preparations for the 2027 election.
summary.nb: Droneangrep fra Sudan dominerer nå det dødelige landskapet, med sudanske droner ansvarlige for nesten tre fjerdedeler av krigsdødsfall i år, og Sør-Sudan anklager Sudan for et droneangrep som drepte tallrike i et omstridt område. Vold fortsetter innenlands, inkludert et veiambush i Warrap som drepte fem personer, en flystyrt på Juba flyplass som etterlot tre overlevende, og en kvinne som angivelig ble slått over en SPLM-primærvalg. Machar oppfordret en spesiell domstol til å sette inn enhetlige styrker i Nasir før kampene i 2025, mens guvernøren i Jonglei provins rapporterte om innsats for å stoppe dødelige sammenstøt i Bor, Duk og Twic East. Nye regulatoriske tiltak inkluderer at SSRA og NCA strammer inn reglene for spill- og gambling-selskaper, og at NEC gir en AU-valg-ekspert en orientering om forberedelsene til valget i 2027.

background.title: South Sudanese Civil War
background.extract: The South Sudanese Civil War was a multi-sided civil war in South Sudan fought from 2013 to 2018 between government and opposition forces. The civil war caused rampant human rights abuses, including forced displacement, ethnic massacres, and killings of journalists by various parties. Since the war's end, South Sudan has been governed by a coalition formed by leaders of the former warring factions, Salva Kiir and Riek Machar. The country continues to recover from the war while experiencing ongoing and systemic ethnic violence.
